sections.heading: C — Dangerous driving behaviors: alcohol, drugs, open containers, children aboard, aggressive and distracted driving
sections.markdown:
## C — Dangerous driving behaviors: alcohol, drugs, open containers, children aboard, aggressive and distracted driving

FACT_ID: sec08-F01 | anchor: A33
Alcohol and drugs impair driving, making it very hard or impossible to drive safely, and drunk or drugged driving threatens everyone on the road. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F02 | anchor: A33
Blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, measures how much alcohol is in your blood. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F03 | anchor: A33
Maryland treats a driver as under the influence of alcohol at a BAC of .08 or above. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F04 | anchor: A33
Any amount of alcohol can hurt your driving: judgment and coordination may suffer well below .08, which can still lead to criminal charges. [A33]
Why it matters: staying under .08 is not a safe harbor.
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F05 | anchor: A33
Even 1 drink can affect your vision, simple movements and reaction time and raise your crash risk. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F06 | anchor: A33
You cannot judge your BAC by counting drinks, because weight, body fat, and when and how much you ate change how your body handles alcohol. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F07 | anchor: A33
Fatigue, mood and medications also change how alcohol affects your driving. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F08 | anchor: A33
Drinking any alcohol at all is illegal for anyone under 21. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F09 | anchor: A33
A driver under 21 who is stopped after drinking will have the license suspended or revoked and may also be charged with breaking the license's alcohol restriction. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F10 | anchor: A33
Driving with an open alcohol container in the passenger area of the vehicle is against the law. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F11 | anchor: A33
An open container is any opened can, bottle, container or package, and a six-pack with open, empty or missing cans or bottles can count as one. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F12 | anchor: A33
The passenger area covers the driver and passenger seats and any spot the driver or passengers can easily reach while seated. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F13 | anchor: A33
Illegal drugs, some prescription medicines and chemical inhalants can badly affect alertness, concentration, coordination and reaction time. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F14 | anchor: A33
All drugs can make it harder to judge distance and to respond to signals and sounds on the road. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F15 | anchor: A33
Driving under the influence of controlled dangerous substances can get your license suspended or revoked. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F16 | anchor: A33
Read prescription and over-the-counter labels for warnings against driving or running heavy machinery; driving impaired against such a warning can bring a criminal charge. [A33]
Source: [A33 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec08-F17 | anchor: A34
If you are convicted of drunk or drugged driving with a child in the vehicle, the judge may double your fine and jail time. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F18 | anchor: A34
Aggressive driving includes speeding, tailgating, ignoring signals and devices, unsafe lane changes, failing to yield and unsafe or illegal passing. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F19 | anchor: A34
Crowded roads, surprise delays, hurrying, construction and stress can push people into driving aggressively. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F20 | anchor: A34
To avoid aggressive-driving incidents, leave extra travel time, stay patient and courteous, and focus on your own driving. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F21 | anchor: A34
Other anti-aggression habits are signaling what you plan to do, obeying all traffic controls, yielding the right-of-way and refusing to compete with other drivers. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F22 | anchor: A34
Safe driving needs constant awareness of the vehicles in front of, behind and beside you. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F23 | anchor: A34
Distracted driving means taking your eyes, your hands or, above all, your mind off driving. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F24 | anchor: A34
Distracted driving causes more police-reported crashes than any other cause. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F25 | anchor: A34
Distractions include eating or drinking, adjusting music or a GPS, handling children or pets, loose objects, phone calls or texting, smoking, makeup, shaving, reading and talking with passengers. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec08-F26 | anchor: A34
A useful rule is to treat other drivers and road users the way you want them to treat you. [A34]
Source: [A34 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0034]

Glossary: BAC — blood alcohol concentration, the measure of alcohol in the blood [A33]. Open container — any opened alcohol can, bottle, container or package [A33]. Passenger area — the seats plus any place occupants can easily reach [A33]. CDS — controlled dangerous substances, meaning illegal drugs and some prescription drugs [A33]. Distracted driving — eyes, hands or mind taken off driving [A34].
Memory aid: if you plan to drink, plan not to drive [A33].
Misconception: counting drinks does not tell you your blood alcohol level; body weight, food, fatigue and medicine all change it [A33].
